images.filename: Ross Friary Side Chapel Armas Cloinne Domhnaill 2010 09 14.jpg
images.caption:
Plaque at the north wall of the side chapel, depicting the coat of arms of the Connacht branch of the Domhnaill family. Transcription of the inscription:

HIS VINCES

ARMAS•CLOINNE
DOMHNAILL•1646


His vinces is the motto on top of the crest, meaning “by these—conquer”. At the center of the shield is a Calvary cross with a waning crescent moon on its dexter side and a right hand on its sinister side above a galleon and a salmon.

images.filename: Ross Friary Choir Memorial Plaque dedicated to Ullick Burke and Kate Lynch 2010 09 14.jpg
images.caption:
Memorial plaque at the right hand side of the high altar in the choir, dedicated to Ullick Burke and his wife Kate Lynch. Transcription of the inscription:

IAN Ye 17 ANNO 1711

GOD BE
MERCIFVLL TO Ye SOULS
OF VLLICK BVRKE & HIS
WIFE KATE LYNCH SO
N TO IOHN BVRKE OF
CASTLE HACKET AND
THEIR POSTERITIE


Translated to modern English: January the 17th anno 1711: God be merciful to the souls of Ullick Burke and his wife Kate Lynch, son to John Burke of Castle Hacket and their posterity.

images.filename: Tuam Cathedral of the Assumption Blessed Virgin Mary and the Four Evangelists by Michael O'Connor 2009 09 14.jpg
images.caption:
Tuam Cathedral of the Assumption, County Galway, Ireland


Upper part of the stained glass window in the chancel. This window was designed by Michael O'Connor of 80 Dame Street, Dublin, in 1832 for £240. The window was restored by the Abbey Stained Glass Studios in Dublin. The lowest shown row of lights depicts the Blessed Virgin Mary (middle window) and the Four Evangelists: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John (from left to right). The next row of ten small lights show the coat of arms of families who helped to finance the cathedral. Among them were Bellew, Blake, Browne, Handcock, Kirwan, Newell, St. George, Shrewsbury, and others. One row of four small orange windows shows the year 1832. Please note that the lowest section of this window is not shown on this photograph as it is obscured by a screen which was erected in 1992. (See Peter Galloway: The Cathedrals of Ireland, ISBN 0-85389-452-3, p. 213–216, and Séan Spellissy: The History of Galway, ISBN 0-9534683-4-8, p. 238–239.)
images.alt:
